title: Declarative version anchoring: SDK & API resolution rules, errors, and fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define unambiguous semantics for 'pinning' a model version from the API and SDK surfaces. This ticket covers how clients may specify model references (tag, semver range, exact semver, commit hash, or hybrid selectors), how the control plane resolves them to a concrete model artifact, and what the SDK/runtime should do on ambiguous or stale pins. Deliverables: API contract examples, SDK helper behavior, resolution precedence matrix, error classes and codes, telemetry fields, and a migration note for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: API spec updated with grammar for model selector field and its allowed forms (tag, semver exact/range, commit hash, alias)
Resolution precedence matrix documented and validated with unit tests and integration tests against the model catalog simulator
SDKs (Python + TS) implement a "resolveModel()" helper consistent with the API and expose clear error types for retryable vs. fatal failures
Runtime implements a stable fallback policy: when pinned model is unavailable, evaluate compatible variants according to documented compatibility windows and emit audit events
Migration guide published describing behavior changes for clients that previously used naive 'latest' strings and guidance to adopt declarative pins
technical_design: - hybrid forms allowed: tag:<t>@semver:<range> or semver:<range>@ref:<hash>
Resolution precedence (highest to lowest): ref (exact commit) -> semver exact -> semver range (latest satisfying) -> tag+semver -> tag alone -> 'latest' (deprecated)

When multiple selectors are provided, the resolver must attempt the left-most selector first and fall back using the precedence rules. The SDK should canonicalize hybrid selectors to an ordered list prior to sending to control plane.

Time-to-resolve / TTL: resolved bindings are cached for 5 minutes by default by SDKs; cache TTL configurable via client options. Cache entries include resolved artifact id and metadata (build SHA, performance profile id, published_at).

Compatibility constraints: control plane stores 'compatibility windows' per model artifact (ABI: tokenizer version, runtime ops, quantization fingerprint). The resolver must only pick artifacts compatible with the requesting runtime profile. If none compatible, return a structured error (ERR_NO_COMPATIBLE_ARTIFACT) with suggested alternates.

Fallback semantics at runtime: if a pinned artifact becomes unhealthy during request processing, runtime should: 1) attempt warm fallback to closest compatible variant (same major semver if within compatibility window), 2) if fallback used, mark request as degraded and tag trace with 'fallback.used', 3) if no fallback available, surface an HTTP 503 with Retry-After and a pinned-resolution error code.
api_examples: Error examples: ERR_AMBIGUOUS_PIN (400): returned when selector matches multiple artifacts with equal precedence and no disambiguator provided; ERR_NO_COMPATIBLE_ARTIFACT (409): when matches exist but none compatible with runtime profile; ERR_PIN_EXPIRED (410): when a previously cached resolution falls outside the artifact's stability window
sdk_migration_guides: Python SDK: add ModelSelector helper. Example: ModelSelector.from_string('tag:stable@semver:^1.3.0').resolve(client) returns a ResolvedModel object with metadata and a 'is_stale' flag.
TS SDK: export canonicalizeSelector(selector: string): string[] which returns an ordered list of candidate selectors the client will send to the control plane

Clients previously passing raw 'model' strings should be opt-in to strict mode via client config `pinning_mode: 'strict' | 'lenient'`. Strict mode returns a helpful error for ambiguous selectors rather than silently picking latest.

Recommend migration path: 1) enable lenient logging to collect which 'latest' artifacts are being used across traffic, 2) choose explicit semver or ref pins for critical routes, 3) enable strict on canary traffic and fix failures before wide rollout
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize API schema and publish spec to docs; SDK scaffolding landed behind feature flags
Week 2: E2E tests with model catalog simulator; add integration tests for ambiguous selector responses
Week 3: Beta release of SDK helpers to plugin customers; collect feedback and telemetry
Week 4: Gradual rollout of control plane enforcement for ambiguous pins (initially warn-only, then 409 on strict)
telemetry_and_audit: Emit 'model.resolve' events with fields: client_id, selector_string, resolved_model_id, resolution_path, latency_ms, cache_hit
Emit 'model.fallback' events when runtime uses a fallback with fields: original_selector, fallback_model_id, reason
Audit log entry for resolved binding changes including who (actor) initiated change, previous resolved artifact, and performance_profile id
dependencies: ENG-10411 (model-catalog: expose artifact metadata + compatibility windows)
PM-402 (document pinning best practices in developer docs)
notes: Decision: deprecated the generic 'latest' selector but will support it with a deprecation window of 6 months
Trade-off: short client-side TTL improves freshness but increases control plane lookups; default 5m chosen as conservative middle ground

Open question: should semver ranges be resolved server-side to the snapshot artifact id at request time or should we introduce a 'binding' resource for long-lived pins? Proposal: implement request-time resolution first and a follow-up ticket for explicit 'binding' resources (pin objects).
